newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner-German banks ready for higher competition.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner-German banks ready for higher competition.

text.p: German banks are well-positioned to cope with the competitive pressures from increased globalisation and by currency union in 1997, a leading German banker said on Tuesday.

"The big German banks, with their different earnings centres, are well-equipped to take advantage of the opportunities offered at home and abroad by the changes in the financial markets," said Juergen Sarrazin, chief executive of Dresdner Bank.

Sarrazin said Dresdner, Germany's second-largest bank, was basing its reaction to competitive changes on four strategic areas -- private banking, corporate banking, investment banking and asset management.
The trend in private banking was towards higher levels of service and customer advice, while services like telebanking and direct banking would continue to grow, said Sarrazin.
New developments in financial instruments and technology would lead to corporate customers being offered a more complex palette of products.
"Investment banking will take on more importance with a view to cross-border acquisitions and takeovers and the expected increase in the number of privatisations," said Sarrazin.
The growth in funds worldwide and the increased necessity for private pension provision meant there was great potential in the asset management area, Sarrazin said.
